open_blockers.claim: The button has no outward stop and no preload, so its rest pose (the flush 'unchanged outer skin' state) is not defined by the geometry. With the designed 0.2 mm stem free play the stem spring cannot hold the button at rest, and nothing stops outward rotation until the rear skin edge wedges into the window edge at about +3.9 deg. At that angle the free end of the face (about 26 mm from the hinge) sits about 1.7 mm proud of the outer skin. No check covers positive rotation, F4 'return to rest' or the F2 behaviour 'moves on one controlled path without rattling'. All rotation checks sweep only negative angles.
evidence: Independent re-measure (CadQuery 2.8, re-imported button/model.step and shell/model.step, rotation about (-12,25,z)): +1 deg d=0.2721 mm; +2 deg d=0.1828 mm at (-10.22,31.26,10.0); +3 deg d=0.0750 mm; +4 deg overlap 0.0080 mm3; +5 deg overlap 0.328 mm3; +8 deg overlap 7.14 mm3. All contacts are at the rear window edge x~-10.4, z=10.0, which is a wedge contact and not a designed stop face.
recipe rotation_checks: press-swept-clearance end_deg -1.865, overtravel-stop-engages and housing-clear-until-stop end_deg -2.665. There is no positive-angle check, and motion_checks is [].
design_parameters.stem_free_play_mm=0.2: rest-plunger-free-play measured 0.19999999999999932 mm, so at rest the plunger does not touch the stem.
FLOW_RESULT 3_function_decomposition F2 behaviour: 'moves on one controlled path without rattling against the shell'; F4: 'returns to rest after release'.
protected_constraints: 'Outer shell skin is not reshaped; the button face is the removed skin piece.' This holds only at the nominal pose, and nothing holds the button there.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Add a rest-defining feature without touching the outer skin. Options: (a) an inner lip on the skin piece or tongue that bears on the inside of the shell (or the tab or stop shelf) at the rest pose; or (b) zero free play with a defined stem preload against an outward stop. State in the recipe which feature defines the rest pose.
open_blockers.required_test: Add a rotation check from 0 to a small positive angle (for example +0.5 deg) against the shell with end_max_distance_mm set, so the outward stop must engage at or just after 0 deg. Also report the face protrusion at the outward stop angle (required <= a stated flushness tolerance). As a negative control, confirm the check FAILS on the current geometry (which swings to about +3.9 deg).

open_blockers.claim: The button cannot be assembled onto the shell. The hinge pin is fused to the shell at BOTH ends (lower tab and upper tab), and the button barrel is a closed ring around it, so the button is captive. The selected concept's stated assembly method ('Button barrel slides over the pin from below before the PCB is fitted'; 'Pin is part of the shell; barrel slides on') is geometrically impossible because the lower tab blocks the barrel. Shell and button are delivered as separate single-solid parts, so print-in-place is not the declared method either, and it would not work as modelled: the button floats with its lowest face (tongue z=7.8) 0.3 mm above the stop shelf (z=7.5) and the barrel 0.8 mm above the lower tab, so it would need support material inside sub-millimetre gaps.
evidence: side_button_recipe.py: pin cylinder from z = bz0-tg-3 = 6.7 to bz1+tg+3 = 21.3; tab_low_box z 6.7..9.7 and tab_high_box z 18.3..21.3 at the pin location; shell_part = union(shell_open, tab_low, tab_high, pin, stop_shelf, stop_post).
button = button_solid minus barrel_bore (radius 1.3, z 9.5..18.5); barrel_outer radius 2.6, z 10.5..17.5, so a closed ring surrounds the pin. Visible as a closed eye in button/iso.png.
measurements.json solid-count-shell = 1 (pin and tabs fused); my re-import: shell volume inside a 4x4x15 box around the pin (z 6.5..21.5) = 123.7 mm3.

My CadQuery translation test on the exported STEP files: moving the button 1 mm along -z gives 26.93 mm3 overlap with the shell, +z 19.93 mm3, +x 14.97, -x 15.14, +y 10.25, -y 8.79 mm3; 3 mm moves overlap 13.6..112.8 mm3. No straight escape direction exists.

open_blockers.claim: Maintained as blocking. ASM2 independently confirms it (first contact at about +3.70 deg by bisection), and so does V1 (+4 deg overlap 0.008 mm3, the same value I measured). The two disagree on severity, and I challenge ASM2 rating it only major. With 0.2 mm free play there is no return to the drawn pose. The face can sit up to about 1.7 mm proud and wedge into a cosmetic edge. F2 ("without rattling") and F4 ("returns to rest") are then unmet by design, not just unverified, and every rest-based check starts from a pose that nothing enforces.

open_blockers.proposed_change: Accepted change: add an outward rest stop at the free end of the face. This is a lip about 1.0 mm deep and 2 mm tall (z) on the inner side of the skin piece, past the window edge at x about 14.4-15.5. At 0 deg it bears on the inner face of the shell wall, so the outer surface is unchanged. The lip moves away from the wall during a press, and it can only be fitted from inside, which is compatible with inserting a pin from the open bottom. Preload: a separate return element (a printed leaf spring from the shell onto the rib, or a small purchased torsion or compression spring), giving a stated preload torque that holds the lip on the shell. The stem must not be the rest-defining element.
open_blockers.required_test: A positive-angle rotation check that ends on lip contact at 0 deg +/- 0.05 deg (end_max_distance small). It must assert that the contact pair is lip to shell inner wall, not the window edge. A static check at rest must show the window edge clear by at least the hinge play plus 0.1 mm. Then a physical rattle and return test on the print.

open_blockers.claim: Upgraded from major to blocking after I reproduced the V2 counterexample. With the barrel offset +0.29 mm in X, inside the designed 0.3 mm radial play, the face edge hits the window edge at x=14.4 already at -1.5 deg. At that angle the stem overlap is only 1.42 mm3 (about 0.36 mm of stem travel, below the 0.5 mm assumed operating travel), against 2.0 mm3 at the nominal press angle. The design's own nominal play can therefore jam the button before it clicks. The offset in -X (-0.29 mm) shows no such contact, so this is one-sided and orientation-dependent, and the centred-axis certificates do not detect it.
evidence: Reviewer read-only CadQuery probe on the exported model.step files (scratchpad script, nothing written to the build folder): translate +0.29 X, rotate about (-11.71,25): -1.0 deg no shell overlap (stem 0.681 mm3); -1.5 deg shell overlap 0.0564 mm3 at x 14.40-14.44, y 28.86-30.21, z 10-16.4 (stem 1.423 mm3); -1.865 deg 0.162 mm3

verification.json V2 reports the same 0.0564 mm3 at (14.4,30.21,10.0); assembly.json ASM3 the same 0.3 mm play-closes-clearances result

open_blockers.proposed_change: Accepted change: a separate Ø2.0 mm ground steel dowel through a tab_low hole into tab_high, inserted from the open bottom. Run it in a button bore printed undersize and drilled or reamed to about Ø2.05-2.1 (radial play of 0.1 mm or less, set by a printed coupon). Then size every running gap (window edge at the press and stop angles, barrel to inner wall, stem free play) as radial play + FDM error + 0.1 mm, using a written stack-up.
open_blockers.required_test: Re-run press-swept, stop-engage and housing-clear with the axis offset to the radial-play limits in +/-X and +/-Y (four runs, or an envelope). All must keep the window edge clear until the stop, and must reach the operating stem travel before any shell contact other than the stop.

open_blockers.claim: I confirm MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN, ASM1 and V4 from the mechanism side. As modelled, the F2 guide cannot be built: the pin is fused to both tabs and the barrel is a closed ring. The fix must be chosen together with R2-M2, because the pin choice sets the hinge play. One manufacturing proposal is challenged: an "M2 screw" as the pivot. A threaded shank running in a printed bore gives a rough bearing with about 0.2-0.3 mm effective radial play at the thread roots, and it wears the bore. That recreates R2-M2. A smooth dowel or shoulder screw is acceptable; a plain threaded screw is not.
evidence: manufacturing.json MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN: section areas 30.0 mm2 at tab levels, 3.142 mm2 pin-only between, so the pin is fused at both ends
assembly.json ASM1: no straight escape direction (1 mm moves overlap 8.8-26.9 mm3)
manufacturing.json proposed_change: "purchased steel dowel or M2 screw"
open_blockers.proposed_change: Use a separate smooth dowel (or shoulder screw) pressed into tab_high and sliding through tab_low, inserted from the open bottom after the button is placed. Do not use a plain threaded screw as the bearing surface.
open_blockers.required_test: An insertion-path check (button placed from inside, then the pin translated along +Z with no overlap except the intended press fit), plus a coupon measurement of the bore and pin fit.

open_blockers.claim: Kept as blocking after cross-check. Mechanism M1 (blocking) and Assembly ASM2 (major) found the same problem independently, and the numbers agree. Nothing defines the rest pose: the stem has 0.2 mm free play and there is no outward stop. Outward rotation is free until an incidental edge wedge at +3.70 deg, where the far face corner is about 1.73 mm proud of the skin. This corrects my round-1 '+3.9 deg'; ASM2's 3.70 deg bisection is confirmed. At that pose the plunger-to-stem gap is about 1.59 mm. The flush 'outer skin unchanged' constraint and every rest-pose check hold only in a pose that no feature enforces.
evidence: Round-2 re-measure (CadQuery 2.8, re-imported exported STEP, read-only scratchpad script): outward first contact by bisection at +3.699 deg (shell distance >0 below, 0 at or above).
Far face corner lever about 26.75 mm (dx 26, dy about 6.3) x 3.699 deg = 1.727 mm outward. Plunger-to-stem gap = 0.2 + 21.5*sin(3.699 deg) = 1.587 mm (confirms ASM2's 'about 1.6 mm').
Round-1 samples, unchanged: +2 deg 0.183 mm, +3 deg 0.075 mm, +4 deg overlap 0.008 mm3, +5 deg overlap 0.328 mm3 (match M1 and ASM2 exactly).
Recipe rotation_checks are all negative-angle; motion_checks is [].
open_blockers.proposed_change: Add a designed outward rest stop inside the skin (a lip on the skin or tongue bearing on the shell inner face, or a lug on the stop post). Define rest by preload against it: either zero stem free play with a stated preload, or a separate return spring. Keep the cosmetic window edge out of the load path.
open_blockers.required_test: Required checks on the revised recipe. (1) rest-stop-engages: rotation 0 to +0.5 deg against the shell, end_max_distance_mm <= 0.02. The closest-point pair must lie on the named stop features, not on the window edge (|x - window edge| > 0.3 mm). (2) outward-flushness: at the stop pose, max outward displacement of the skin-piece outer surface relative to the original skin <= a stated tolerance (for example 0.1 mm). (3) rest-preload-or-retention: stem contact distance <= 0 under the stated preload, or a stated retention feature. (4) Negative control: run check (1) on the CURRENT geometry and confirm it FAILS (current first contact is at +3.70 deg on the window edge).

open_blockers.claim: Upgraded from major to blocking. This is not to agree with ASM1 and MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN; the measured geometry shows the two declared separate parts cannot be assembled at all, so the deliverable as specified cannot exist physically. The pin is fused to the shell at both ends and the barrel is a closed ring between the tabs. Every straight escape direction overlaps the shell, and the selected concept's 'barrel slides over the pin from below' is geometrically impossible.
evidence: Round-2 re-measure (CadQuery 2.8, re-imported exported STEP, read-only scratchpad script): shell cross-section in box x -15..-9, y 23..27: 24.0 mm2 at z 6.8, 8.0 and 9.65 (tab), 3.142 mm2 (pin only, r=1.0) at z 9.75, 14 and 18.2, and 24.0 mm2 at z 18.35 and 21.2. The pin is continuous and fused to both tabs. This confirms MFG's pattern; MFG's 30.0 mm2 figure comes from a different box and I did not reproduce that exact value.
Shell volume in box x -14..-10, y 23..27, z 6.5..21.5 = 123.686 mm3. Confirms ASM1's 123.7 mm3; hand check 96 (tabs) + 27.0 (pin span) = 123.0 plus the pin inside the box edges.
1 mm translations of the button, overlap with the shell: +x 14.965, -x 15.141, +y 10.253, -y 8.789, -z 26.930, +z 19.933 mm3. All six of ASM1's values are confirmed to 0.01 mm3.

open_blockers.required_test: Required checks. (1) insertion-path: a translation (or translation plus rotation) motion check of the button, with any separate pin absent, from a pose fully outside the cavity along the declared vector to the rest pose. It must show zero overlap with the shell, or a stated, bounded snap interference with its own check. (2) pin-insertion: a translation check of the separate pin along its axis through the tab holes with zero overlap. (3) retention: once the retainer or pin is fitted, a translation of the button along the reverse insertion vector must overlap (a negative test that proves capture). open_blockers.claim: I confirm ASM1, MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN and V4. The CAD contradicts the chosen concept's own stated assembly method, which says 'Button barrel slides over the pin from below before the PCB is fitted' and 'Pin is part of the shell; barrel slides on'. The three reviewers' translation probes are sample counterexamples. The stronger argument comes straight from the recipe and is topological. The pin (z 6.7-21.3) is unioned with tab_low and tab_high, which are unioned with the skin into one shell solid (solid-count-shell = 1). The pin therefore forms a closed loop through the shell. The barrel is a closed ring (bore r1.3 for the whole barrel height) linked around that loop. No rigid motion of any kind can separate the two separately printed parts, so the prototype cannot be built as delivered. From the requirements side, this is the designer's own contract failing. It is not an owner preference.
evidence: recipe op shell_part = union(shell_open, tab_low, tab_high, pin, stop_shelf, stop_post); pin origin z 6.7, height 14.6; tab_low z 6.7-9.7, tab_high z 18.3-21.3
recipe outputs: shell and button are separate parts, each expected_solids 1; measurements solid-count-shell actual 1

Whether an extra purchased part (dowel or clip) is acceptable is an owner decision. Note that it changes the 3-part count used to justify the selection (see R2-selection-rationale-collapses).

open_blockers.claim: I confirm M1 and V1 as blocking. I disagree with ASM2 rating the same defect only major, for a requirements reason. The only protected constraint is 'Outer shell skin is not reshaped; the button face is the removed skin piece', and it rests on the user's explicit '外形はできるだけ変えないで' (keep the outer shape as unchanged as possible). That constraint holds only in a nominal pose that no feature enforces. Three independent probes put first outward contact at about 3.5-4 deg (M1), 3.70 deg (ASM2) and 3.9 deg (V1). These are numerically consistent: about 26-26.7 mm x sin(3.7-3.9 deg) gives 1.7-1.8 mm. So the far edge of the face can sit about 1.7 mm proud of the skin in normal use. The hinge axis is vertical (+Z), so gravity does not restore rotation, and the stem has 0.2 mm free play, so nothing returns the face to flush. I also challenge one of the proposed fixes. M1(b) and V1(b) propose 'zero free play with a stated stem preload'. That sets a value tied to real switch force and dimensions, which the user explicitly asked to leave undetermined. It also conflicts with ASM3/V2, because the designed 0.3 mm hinge play would then turn into uncontrolled preload or pre-travel. Fix (a), a designed internal outward stop, is the requirements-compatible route.
evidence: recipe.protected_constraints and request text SRC-1 '外形はできるだけ変えないで' and '実スイッチ寸法・押下力・クリック感は未確定として残す'

open_blockers.proposed_change: Add an internal outward rest stop (lip or tab on the skin piece, rib or tongue bearing on the inside of the shell or tabs at 0 deg), keeping the outer skin untouched. If a return or preload element is needed, choose one whose force does not depend on the undetermined switch (for example the R_spring option already in the portfolio), or state any switch-dependent preload as an owner-pending assumption. State the allowed flushness or rattle tolerance as an owner question, not a designer-fixed number.
open_blockers.required_test: A positive-direction rotation check (0 to about +0.5 deg) requiring designed contact at the new stop near 0 deg. Run it against the current geometry as a negative control: it must fail there, since the button swings to about +3.7-3.9 deg. Also run the outer-surface deviation check from R2-outer-preservation-unmeasured at the outward-stop pose.

open_blockers.claim: Kept and confirmed by ASM1-no-insertion-path and V4-assembly-claim-contradicts-cad. Their independent translation probes (no escape direction; overlap at dz +/-0.4 mm) agree with my shell sections (pin-only 3.142 mm2 at z 9.75-18.2, solid tab at both ends). I evaluated the proposed routes for printability. Rejected: (1) ASM1 option (c), a C-shaped snap barrel on the printed pin. The pin is a 2.0 mm column printed along the build axis, and the snap-on side load bends it across layer lines. The snap interference also depends on uncalibrated FDM hole and pin size. (2) V4's print-in-place option. The tongue sits 0.3 mm above the shelf and the skin in a 0.4 mm window gap, so support would be trapped in sub-millimetre gaps. Accepted: ASM1 option (b) / V4 'separate pin through tab holes'. The pin goes in from below through tab_low after the button is placed from inside the cavity. The bore is printed slightly undersize and drilled to the pin after printing.
evidence: ASM1 and V4: no translation escape path; V4 overlaps at dz +/-0.4 mm and +/-12 mm.
My shell sections: area 30.0 mm2 at z 6.8-9.65 and 18.35-21.2, 3.142 mm2 at z 9.75-18.2.
Recipe: tongue_z_min 7.8 vs stop_shelf_z_max 7.5 (0.3 mm), window_gap_mm 0.4: support for print-in-place would sit in these gaps.
Recipe pin_radius_mm 1.0, pin axis = z = shell build axis in either practical shell orientation.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Part split: shell (printed), button (printed), pin (stock). The pin is either a cut length of 1.75 mm filament, which needs no purchase and is axially oriented, or a 2 mm steel dowel, which is a purchased part and should be recorded as one. Put through-holes in tab_low and blind or through holes in tab_high. Print the barrel bore and tab holes about one drill size under, then drill to the chosen pin after printing. Write the sequence into the recipe: button in from the open bottom, pin in along +z through tab_low, then switch/PCB.
open_blockers.required_test: CAD insertion-path check: the button with no pin moves from inside the cavity to rest, then the pin moves along +z through tab_low, both with zero overlap against shell, shelf and stop post. Physical check: drill-to-fit coupon (a printed bore plus tab hole on the chosen pin) with measured radial play reported.

open_blockers.claim: I confirm M1-no-outward-rest-stop / ASM2-rest-pose-not-located / V1-rest-pose-unconstrained. My own probe: outward rotation about (-12,25,z) gives 0.1828 mm at +2 deg, 0.075 at +3, 0.0213 at +3.5, first overlap at +3.8 deg (0.0004 mm3), i.e. the cosmetic window edge is the only outward limit. However, two of the proposed fixes are hard to make by FDM. (a) M1 option (b), 'stem free play 0 with stated preload', makes the rest pose depend on printed tolerances: the 0.3 mm designed hinge play (M2/ASM3/V2) and FDM placement error are both larger than any preload window, so a printed part will be either pre-actuated or loose. This directly conflicts with ASM3/V2, which require free play to exceed the stack. (b) ASM2/V1 'inner lip on the skin piece bearing on the inside of the shell' gives rest flushness set by two printed curved surfaces. If the lip projects above z 18 it also destroys the flat build face proposed below. It also makes the button larger than the window, so it must enter from inside (compatible with MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN only if the insertion path is checked).
evidence: My CadQuery outward rotation probe (read-only, exported STEP): +2 deg 0.1828 mm, +3 deg 0.0750 mm, +3.5 deg 0.0213 mm, +3.8 deg overlap 0.0004 mm3, +4 deg 0.0080 mm3, matching M1 (~3.5-4 deg), ASM2 (3.70 deg) and V1 (~3.9 deg).
Recipe stem_free_play_mm 0.2 vs pin/bore radial play 0.3 (pin_radius 1.0, barrel_inner_radius 1.3).
ASM3: switch-position tolerance window about -0.2/+0.3 mm, same size as hinge play.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Make rest a hard outward stop with faces normal to y, built as vertical walls in the build orientation so their position is set by XY accuracy, not by layer height. Example: a second face on the stop post (or a shell lug on the shelf) on the +y side of the tongue, capturing the tongue between the overtravel face and the rest face with stated running clearance. Preload the button against it with a compliant element whose deflection is much larger than the tolerance stack. Options are an integral printed leaf on the button bending in the XY plane (layers along its length) bearing on the shell interior, or a small purchased spring. Keep the stem free play as a positive gap. Do not use a stem preload.
open_blockers.required_test: Positive-angle rotation check with end_max_distance on the designed rest-stop pair (not the window edge). Repeat it with the button offset by the hinge play envelope. On a printed sample, measure face protrusion at rest and the rest-to-actuation free play with a feeler gauge.

open_blockers.claim: I confirm the captive-hinge blocker (MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN, V4) and add three things measured on the exported STEP files. (1) A separate pin, the fix that MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN and my own R1 proposed, is necessary but not sufficient. Even with the printed pin removed, the shell-integral stop post sits directly inboard (-y) of the stop tongue and blocks the only workable insertion path, a +y slide from inside the shell. (2) The 'open-ended pin, barrel slides on axially' route (V4 option and my R1 option a) is invalid for this layout. The skin piece sits in the window with about 0.3 mm of z clearance, so the button cannot travel axially along any pin by its 7 mm barrel length. (3) Insertion from outside through the window is impossible because the barrel (x -14.6..-9.4) lies outside the window opening (x -10.4..14.4). Under the current shell geometry no fix limited to the pin produces an assemblable product.
evidence: Probe (CadQuery 2.8, BRepExtrema distance + boolean overlap on shell/button model.step; printed pin between tabs subtracted to simulate a separate pin): pure +y translation of the button at dz=0 is blocked for dy in [-6,-1.2] mm; overlap 8.71 mm3 at dy=-3, 3.91 at -2, 1.03 at -1.4, 0 at -1.1. Every overlap lies in x 10.5..13.5, y <=23.81, z 7.8..9.4, which is the tongue against stop_post.

Same probe with the stop_post box also subtracted: +y path from dy=-11 to 0 is clear at every sample (min distance 0.30 mm, limited by the skin top edge z=18 vs tab_high underside z=18.3; 0.272 at rest).

Search around the post with the pin removed: at dy=-1.19 and dy=-1.6 no offset with dx in {-3.5,-3,-2,0,2,3,3.5} and dz in {-2,-1.7,0,1.7,2} is collision-free, so a translation that sidesteps the post was not found (coarse grid, not a proof of none).

Axial route: round-1 probe moving the button +z 1 mm gives 19.93 mm3 overlap and -z 1 mm 26.93 mm3, and +z 0.3 mm already reaches contact (skin top on tab_high). A 7 mm slide along the pin axis is impossible regardless of which tab is removed.
Recipe: barrel_outer r 2.6 at hinge x=-12 gives x -14.6..-9.4, and window_gap x -10.4..14.4, so the barrel cannot pass through the window from outside.
Probe: a vertical lift from below the open bottom at dy=-11 (pin and post removed) is clear from dz=-20 to 0 (min 2.6 mm). At dy=-8 the skin piece hits the stop shelf (distance 0 at dz -3..-1).
Probe: a 2 mm diameter corridor along the pin axis below tab_low (z -1..5.6) has 0.0 mm3 overlap with the shell, so a separate pin can be inserted from the open bottom.
MFG-CAPTIVE-PIN required_test and manufacturing remaining_uncertainties already flag that the tongue must clear the stop shelf/post. This probe shows it does not.
open_blockers.proposed_change: Assembly order I would accept for this layout: (1) Print the shell without the integral pin and without the stop post and shelf. Make a Ø2 through-hole in tab_low and a blind hole in tab_high on the hinge axis (-12,25), with a lead-in chamfer at the barrel bore ends. (2) Bring the button in through the open bottom about 11 mm inboard (dy≈-11), lift it to its z band, and slide it +y about 11 mm until a designed outward rest stop seats (see R2-ASM2). The barrel enters between the tabs. (3) Insert a separate pin (steel dowel or M2 screw) from below through tab_low, the barrel and tab_high, and retain it with a press fit in tab_high or a screw head under tab_low. (4) Install from below a switch/stop carrier (PCB bracket) that locates on the pin's lower end or the tab_low hole and carries both the switch and the overtravel stop face. That stop face then approaches the tongue in +z, not along the insertion path. (5) Install the PCB/base. Alternative: keep the stop on the shell but make it a separate snap-in or screw-in post fitted after step 3. Any shell-integral stop that faces +y (resists inward motion) is incompatible with step 2.
open_blockers.required_test: Add sequential path checks that mirror the declared order: (a) button-only translation path (lift at the stated dy, then +y to rest) against the shell with the pin and carrier absent, as a swept/continuous check with min_mm >= a stated assembly clearance; (b) pin translation along +z through tab_low, barrel and tab_high with zero overlap except the declared press-fit zone; (c) carrier translation along +z to its seat with zero overlap against the installed button and shell; (d) re-run all rest, press, stop and housing checks on the final assembly. As a negative control, (a) must FAIL on the current shell (stop post present).

open_blockers.claim: Nothing holds the button at its drawn rest pose. The return element (switch stem) has 0.2 mm designed free play, so it cannot push the button back to rest, and no part stops outward (+) rotation. In my probe the button turns outward with no contact until about 3.5-4 deg. First contact is the near-hinge end face of the skin piece wedging into the window edge (x=-10.4). At that point the far end of the face sticks out about 1.6-1.8 mm. So the button rattles across about 0.2 mm inward plus 1.6 mm or more outward, and its rest position is set by a cosmetic edge rubbing. This breaks F2 ("without rattling") and F4 ("returns to rest"). Every check starts from a pose that no feature enforces.
evidence: recipe rest-plunger-free-play: button-to-stem 0.200 mm at rest, stem is the only return element (F4)
rotation_checks sweep only negative angles (end_deg -1.865 / -2.665); there is no check at positive angles and motion_checks is empty

Reviewer read-only CadQuery probe on exported shell/button/switch_stem model.step (scratchpad script, nothing written to build folder): rotating the button about (-12,25,z) by +2 deg gives a shell distance of 0.183 mm; +3 deg gives 0.075 mm; +4 deg gives 0.008 mm3 of overlap at x=-10.43..-10.40, y=30.8..31.25, z=10..12.9 (skin end against the window edge); +5 deg gives 0.33 mm3 of overlap
button/iso.png and shell/iso.png show no retention lip, hook or outward stop
open_blockers.proposed_change: Add a positive outward stop that defines rest. Two options: (a) put a stop face on the arm, tongue or rib that bears on a shell lug at 0 deg, and preload the button against it with a small spring or flexure; or (b) set stem free play to 0 with a stated stem preload, so the stem holds the button on that stop. Keep the cosmetic window edge out of the load path.
open_blockers.required_test: Add a positive-angle rotation check that requires end contact at a designed rest angle (end_max_distance_mm small) on the new stop feature and not on the window edge. Then show that at rest the plunger and stem are either in contact under preload or held by the stop, and give the outward play in mm at the face.

status.policy: Role coverage is not independent validation; current-revision geometry and unresolved physical requirements remain visible.
unverified_requirements: 押しやすさ（押下力・ストローク感・クリック感）は実機試験していない。
Switch housing, stem position, operating force and travel are assumed placeholders, not a measured switch.
PCB position and the real mouse shell were not measured; this is a stand-in shell.
Hinge play, wear, print tolerance and stiffness of the 1.5 mm skin are not qualified.
Hard-stop stiffness, impact and wear are not modeled; only rigid end-pose contact is checked.
Wall checks are sampled minima of the stated parts, not a proof of minimum wall or of strength.
